title: Complex numbers (just enough for ñ)
summary: A complex number packs two real numbers into one. In ñ = n + iκ the real part sets the speed of light in the material, the imaginary part how fast it fades.

diagrams.title: What n and κ do to a light wave
diagrams.tryThis: Raise n and watch the wave get shorter inside the material; then raise κ and watch it fade faster.

checks.prompt: For c-Si at 650 nm, $\tilde n = 3.84 + 0.015i$. Which number determines how strongly the light is absorbed?

options.feedback: Correct: α = 4πκ/λ₀ depends only on κ.
n sets the speed (and wavelength) inside the material and the reflection at its surface, not the absorption.
The magnitude mixes the two effects; absorption depends on κ alone.
The ratio has no direct physical meaning here; α = 4πκ/λ₀.

hints: Which formula on the sheet contains κ?
κ is the imaginary part of ñ.
solution: $\tilde n = n + i\kappa$: real part n = 3.84, imaginary part κ = 0.015.

checks.prompt: Using $\tilde n = 3.84 + 0.015i$ at λ₀ = 650 nm, calculate α in cm⁻¹ (book ex. 7.5a).
solution: $\alpha = \frac{4\pi \times 0.015}{6.50 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{cm}} = 2.90 \times 10^3$ cm⁻¹ (= 2.9 × 10⁵ m⁻¹, as in the answer book).
